title: The Unexpected Ways GLP-1s Are Transforming Consumer Behavior
gist: A BCG Center for Customer Insight survey of 1,500+ GLP-1 users across nine markets finds the drugs reallocate rather than destroy consumer demand: food dollars shift toward functional, high-protein and high-fiber items while candy, salty snacks, alcohol and soft drinks fall ~10-14%, and freed-up spend flows into supplements (+20%), apparel (+19% casual clothing) and aesthetics. The addressable market is far bigger than active users alone — 16M US users today heading to 30-35M by 2030, roughly 50% larger once household spillover is counted, with about a third of ever-users lapsed at any time and ~60% of those planning to restart.

insights.claim: The active US GLP-1 user base has roughly tripled since 2022 to approximately 16 million people and is projected to reach 30 million to 35 million by 2030 as Medicare obesity coverage begins in 2026 and more employer plans opt in.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: A roughly 2x user-base doubling by 2030 is the sizing input for any consumer-staples or wellness thesis; reimbursement milestones (Medicare 2026, employer opt-ins) are the datable catalysts to track.
insights.quote: The active user base in the US has roughly tripled since 2022, reaching approximately 16 million today.
insights.locator: A Market Driven by Momentum, Not Just Growth

themes.theme: Lapse-and-restart churn as a recurring market

insights.claim: At any given moment roughly one-third of everyone who has ever taken a GLP-1 is lapsed, but approximately 60% of lapsed users plan to restart and more than 10% of active users already cycle on and off intentionally.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Prescription-count time series understate the true consumer cohort; models built on active scripts alone will misjudge both the size and the persistence of GLP-1-linked demand.
insights.quote: At any given moment, roughly one-third of ever-users are lapsed—meaning they have stopped their medication.
insights.locator: What makes this market unusual is its dynamism

insights.claim: GLP-1 adoption behaves as a recurring pool of re-entry rather than a one-time adoption curve, because the main reasons users stop — hitting goal weight or affordability — are both reversible.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Falling drug prices directly convert one of the two main churn drivers into re-entry, so price declines should be read as volume-additive rather than purely margin-dilutive.
insights.quote: This creates a recurring pool of re-entry, instead of a one-time adoption curve.
insights.locator: But this exit is not permanent

insights.claim: After a GLP-1 user lapses, food cravings and old eating habits return within one to three months, but supplement, fitness and personal-care behaviors prove far more durable.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: The durable-behavior categories (supplements, fitness, personal care) hold their incremental demand through churn, making them structurally better exposure than snack-category short trades that mean-revert in a quarter.
insights.quote: Brands positioned at those inflection points capture demand that outlasts any individual prescription.
insights.locator: What happens after a usage lapse is especially important

insights.claim: GLP-1 users expect roughly one-third of the money freed up by eating less to go to savings, one-third to cover GLP-1 co-pays, and only the remaining third to be redirected into supplements, beauty and personal care, apparel, fitness and aesthetics.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Only about a third of the food-spend release actually reaches other consumer categories — a useful haircut on bullish 'GLP-1 wallet shift' sizing for beauty and apparel names.
insights.quote: In other words, the demand will be reallocated, not destroyed.
insights.locator: How GLP-1s Are Reshaping Diets, Spending, and Identity

insights.claim: Active GLP-1 users plan to spend 15% more per month on fruits and vegetables and 11% more on high-protein foods, plus substantially more on high-fiber and whole-grain products.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Fresh produce, protein and fiber suppliers get a volume tailwind that survives user lapse — this is the 'sustained growth' end of the basket.
insights.locator: Active users report they plan to spend 15% more

insights.claim: GLP-1 users say they plan to cut spending 14% on candy and 12% on prepared frozen sides, with salty snacks, alcohol, soft drinks and chocolate each falling roughly 10%, consumed less often and in smaller portions.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: A stated ~10-14% spend cut across indulgence categories is a direct top-line headwind for confectionery, salty-snack, beer/spirits and CSD exposure as the user base doubles.
insights.quote: The flip side is equally pronounced: users say they plan to spend 14% less on candy and 12% less on prepared frozen sides.
insights.locator: The flip side is equally pronounced

insights.claim: GLP-1 users are twice as likely to choose functional products emphasizing health benefits as they are to choose premium options, which favors reformulation around function over simple premiumization.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Portfolios built on price-mix premiumization face a demand mix that rewards protein/fiber functionality instead — watch which staples pivot innovation budgets accordingly.
insights.locator: Respondents reported they will be twice as likely

insights.claim: The GLP-1 spending shift is not yet visible at retail: users are cutting calories without cutting total food spending, and grocers report they are mainly trading up to health-conscious or premium alternatives so far.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Survey intent is running ahead of scanner data, so the absence of a visible grocery hit today is not evidence the shift isn't coming — but it also means the trade has no confirmed catalyst yet.
insights.quote: While GLP-1 users are cutting total calorie consumption, they are not cutting overall food spending, for example.
insights.locator: Not all of our research findings are noticeable on retail shelves yet

insights.claim: GLP-1 users plan to reduce spending across every restaurant format — cafes, fine dining, casual dining and fast casual — ordering smaller portions, lighter options and less alcohol when they do go out.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: The hit lands on ticket size and alcohol attach rate as much as on traffic — margin-negative for restaurant operators whose profit sits in beverage mix.
insights.locator: GLP-1 users also plan to change their spending on food away from home

insights.claim: When GLP-1 users lapse, restaurant visits recover but not to prior frequency, and the fastest recovery is expected at fast casual and quick service restaurants.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: QSR and fast casual have the shortest demand-recovery half-life after lapse; fine and casual dining carry the more permanent frequency impairment.
insights.quote: The fastest recovery is expected to be at fast casual and quick service restaurants.
insights.locator: When users lapse, outside dining picks back up

insights.claim: Active GLP-1 users say they will spend around 20% more on protein and fiber supplements and collagen, with multivitamins, hydration products and hair and skin supplements among the other big gainers.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Supplements combine the largest stated spend increase with post-lapse durability — the highest-quality long exposure the survey identifies.
insights.quote: The supplement aisle is poised to be one of the clearest winners.
insights.locator: The supplement aisle is poised to be one

insights.claim: Supplement demand from GLP-1 users is driven by two reinforcing mechanisms: appetite suppression forces deliberate nutrition, and the medication itself catalyzes a broader shift toward health tracking and optimization.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: The behavioral (tracking/optimization) channel is what makes the supplement uplift outlive the prescription — it is a habit change, not a side-effect workaround.
insights.locator: This pattern reflects both genuine need

insights.claim: Active GLP-1 users expect to spend 19% more on casual clothing, 15% more on footwear and 10% more on active and leisurewear as their body size changes.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Apparel and footwear get a replacement-cycle windfall that scales with the user base — a rarely modeled second-order beneficiary of obesity drugs.
insights.quote: As their bodies change, so will the contents of their closets.
insights.locator: The changes extend well beyond food

insights.claim: GLP-1 users split into four purchase archetypes — lifestyle optimizers (41%), disease managers (27%), aesthetic transformers (19%) and 'all-in' consumers (13%) — each with a distinct spending pattern and go-to-market logic.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: The 41% lifestyle-optimizer plurality is where fitness memberships, wearables and apparel demand concentrates, so segment mix — not headline user count — determines which categories actually get the dollars.
insights.quote: Winning in this space means targeting distinct segments and their unique needs explicitly rather than treating GLP-1 users as a single homogeneous consumer.
insights.locator: Four Archetypes of GLP-1 Consumers

insights.claim: 70% of surveyed GLP-1 users report food and fitness behavior changes among the people they live with, and non-users in those households adopt 30% to 50% of the user's behavioral changes.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: The behavioral contagion inside households is the single largest under-modeled multiplier on GLP-1 consumer impact — it applies to snack and CSD downside as much as to protein upside.
insights.locator: Consider the household effect

insights.claim: Counting household members, the addressable market for GLP-1-influenced consumer demand is roughly 50% larger than the active-user population alone.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Apply a ~1.5x multiplier to active-user counts when sizing GLP-1 exposure; 16M active users today implies roughly 24M behaviorally affected consumers.
insights.quote: That means the addressable GLP-1-driven market is larger than most consumer companies realize.
insights.locator: And shifting consumption patterns extend beyond individual users

insights.claim: Consumer categories sort into four post-GLP-1 trajectories: rebound (salty snacks, frozen meals, candy return to prior levels after stopping), sustained growth (meat, fruits, vegetables, high-protein foods like yogurt), temporary growth (health and wellness foods that revert), and sustained decline (sports drinks and dairy).
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: This is the actionable long/short map: sports drinks and dairy carry permanent impairment while salty snacks and candy are cyclical rebounders that mean-revert on lapse.
insights.locator: Rebound. Products in this group often are consumed

insights.claim: Companies should selectively adjust exposure to rebounding categories such as salty snacks and soft drinks and offer smaller pack sizes in premium and indulgent categories for users trading up within an unchanged budget.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Smaller pack sizes at premium price points is the specific margin defense to watch for in indulgence portfolios — price/mix substituting for lost volume.
insights.locator: Reframe the portfolio around function

insights.claim: GLP-1 medication prices are already declining sharply before patents expire despite there being only two major manufacturers, and are expected to fall further as generics enter and distribution channels shift.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Pre-patent-cliff price erosion in a duopoly is an unusual signal — bearish for incumbent manufacturer pricing power, bullish for the volume of downstream consumer exposure.
insights.quote: At the same time, medication prices are already declining sharply—even before patents expire—an unusual dynamic given there are only two major manufacturers.
insights.locator: Another reason growth in GLP-1 consumption is structural

insights.claim: Oral GLP-1 formats are already in market creating new price tiers, and monthly dosing formulations in development could meaningfully improve adherence.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Better adherence shrinks the lapsed one-third of ever-users, which mechanically raises the persistent share of the behavioral demand shift.
insights.quote: In short, the future of GLP-1s appears clear: more patients, at lower cost, through more formats.
insights.locator: Manufacturers are in the market now with oral formats

insights.claim: Regulators could substantially expand the medically eligible GLP-1 population, with approvals granted or in late-stage review for cardiovascular risk, sleep apnea and metabolic liver disease.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Label expansion into cardio-metabolic indications is the mechanism that unlocks insurance coverage beyond weight loss and underwrites the 30-35M by 2030 path.
insights.locator: Furthermore, regulators could considerably expand the population

insights.claim: Europe and Asia-Pacific GLP-1 patient growth is projected to outpace the US over the next five years, and one-quarter to one-third of aware non-users in China and India express interest in trying the drugs — more than double the 14% US rate, with cost and safety the primary barriers.
insights.speaker: Alex Caffey
insights.so_what: Emerging-Asia latent demand is 2x the US rate and gated on price, so the ongoing price decline converts directly into international volume — the US behavioral shift is a leading indicator for global consumer portfolios.
insights.quote: Roughly one-quarter to one-third of non-users in China and India who are aware of GLP-1s express interest in trying them—more than double the 14% rate in the US.
insights.locator: The GLP-1 Consumer Market Is Set to Greatly Expand
